questions.stem: India celebrates National Sports Day on 29 August each year to honour the birth anniversary of which sporting legend?

options.option_text: Milkha Singh, nicknamed the 'Flying Sikh' of Indian athletics
Major Dhyan Chand, legendary wizard of Indian field hockey
P.T. Usha, known as the 'Payyoli Express' of Indian sprinting
Kapil Dev, who led India to the 1983 Cricket World Cup title

questions.explanation: Major Dhyan Chand (born 29 August 1905) is regarded as the greatest field hockey player in history, winning three Olympic gold medals for India (1928, 1932, 1936). The Government of India declared 29 August as National Sports Day in 2012. Milkha Singh, P.T. Usha, and Kapil Dev are celebrated Indian sportspersons but do not have National Sports Day associated with their birthdays.

questions.stem: World AIDS Day has been observed globally every year on which date, making it the first-ever global health day marked by WHO?

options.option_text: 15 October — falls within the global health awareness calendar
1 December — first observed in 1988 as a WHO-backed initiative
14 November — same month as several other global health days
20 November — coincides with Universal Children's Day observance

questions.explanation: World AIDS Day is observed on 1 December every year since 1988, making it the first-ever global health day designated by WHO. It was proposed by WHO officials James Bunn and Thomas Netter. The other dates are real observances: 15 October is Global Handwashing Day, 14 November is World Diabetes Day, and 20 November is Universal Children's Day — none of which is World AIDS Day.

questions.stem: World Ozone Day is observed on 16 September each year to mark the signing anniversary of which international agreement?

options.option_text: Vienna Convention for Protection of the Ozone Layer, 1985
Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer, 1987
Kyoto Protocol on Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Climate, 1997
Paris Agreement on Climate Action and Global Warming, 2015

questions.explanation: World Ozone Day commemorates the signing of the Montreal Protocol on 16 September 1987, which set binding phase-out schedules for ozone-depleting substances (CFCs, HCFCs). The Vienna Convention (1985) is the most tempting distractor — it addressed ozone protection in principle but set no binding targets; the Protocol did. Kyoto (1997) and Paris (2015) address greenhouse gases, not the ozone layer specifically.

questions.stem: India's 'Rashtriya Matdata Diwas' (National Voters' Day) is observed on 25 January each year to commemorate the founding anniversary of which institution?

options.option_text: National Human Rights Commission, established in October 1993
Election Commission of India, established on 25 January 1950
Delimitation Commission of India, first constituted in 1952
Central Information Commission, established under RTI Act 2005

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950 — one day before India became a Republic. National Voters' Day has been observed on 25 January since 2011 (the 61st ECI founding anniversary) to encourage voter registration among new electors. The Delimitation Commission, NHRC, and CIC are all real statutory bodies, but none was founded on 25 January, making them plausible yet incorrect distractors.

questions.stem: World Population Day is observed on 11 July each year. Which specific global demographic milestone reached on that date in 1987 inspired the United Nations to establish this observance?

options.option_text: World population reached 4 billion, crossing a key growth threshold
World population reached 5 billion, alerting the UN to act urgently
World population reached 6 billion, alarming demographers worldwide
World population reached 3 billion for the second time in history

questions.explanation: On 11 July 1987, the world population crossed 5 billion — a milestone that drew global attention. The UN Development Programme Governing Council adopted World Population Day in 1989, anchoring the date to this 'Five Billion Day.' 4 billion was reached in 1974 (long before 1987), 6 billion in 1999. Option D ('3 billion for the second time') is absurd since each population milestone is crossed only once.

questions.stem: The Government of India formally declared 22 December as National Mathematics Day in which year, and to honour whose birth anniversary?

options.option_text: 2011, honouring C.V. Raman on the centenary of his Nobel Prize win
2012, honouring Srinivasa Ramanujan on his 125th birth anniversary
2010, honouring Aryabhata on 1,500 years since his Aryabhatiya text
2012, honouring P.C. Mahalanobis alongside National Statistics Day

questions.explanation: PM Manmohan Singh declared 22 December as National Mathematics Day on 26 February 2012, to mark the 125th birth anniversary of Srinivasa Ramanujan (born 22 Dec 1887). Option A (C.V. Raman) is the sharpest distractor — National Science Day (28 Feb) does honour Raman for the Raman Effect, but that is a different day. Option D (P.C. Mahalanobis) tempts because National Statistics Day (29 June) does honour him, but those are separate observances.

questions.stem: Unlike most UN observances that fall on a fixed calendar date, 'World Habitat Day' is marked on a variable date each year. Which option correctly states its scheduling rule?

options.option_text: First Sunday of October, dedicated to the spirit of community rest
First Monday of October, per UN General Assembly Resolution 40/202
Second Monday of October, coinciding with World Mental Health Day
Last Monday of September, preceding the October awareness season

questions.explanation: UN General Assembly Resolution 40/202 (1985) established World Habitat Day on the first Monday of October, first observed in 1986 — one of the few UN days tied to a weekday formula rather than a fixed date. Option C is wrong on two counts: World Mental Health Day is 10 October (a fixed date, not the second Monday), and Habitat Day falls on the first — not second — Monday. Options A and D describe invented formulas with no UN basis.
